title: Unit needs inspection (general error)

steps: Switch the unit off with the remote control.
Switch off the air conditioner's circuit breaker or unplug it.
Wait about 5 minutes, then restore power and switch on again.
technician: If CH00 returns after a power reset, request an LG technician.

title: Drain problem or condensate tank full
causes: The indoor drain is not working (ceiling units).
On window and portable units, the condensate tank is full, often on humid days.
steps: Switch off and unplug the unit.
On window or portable units, put a pan of about 1.5 L under the drain port at the lower back and remove the drain cap.
Let the water drain, then refit the cap firmly.
You can fit a drain hose to drain continuously; make sure water does not drip onto anyone below.
technician: If CH04/FL appears often even in dry weather, or on a ceiling unit after a reset, book LG service.

title: Indoor–outdoor communication error
causes: The indoor and outdoor units cannot communicate.
Wiring problem after a new install or move.
steps: Switch the unit off with the remote control.
Switch off the air conditioner's circuit breaker or unplug it.
Wait about 5 minutes, then restore power and switch on again.
technician: If the code stays after a reset, or the unit was just installed or moved, request service.

title: Operating mode conflict
causes: Two indoor units on one system are set to opposite modes (heating vs cooling/dry).
steps: Set all indoor units to heating, or all to cooling/dry.
Fan and air purification modes can run with any mode.
technician: If the code stays with all units on the same mode, contact LG support.

title: Indoor fan problem

Check the indoor unit air filters and clean them if they are dusty.
Switch off the air conditioner's circuit breaker or unplug it.
Wait about 5 minutes, then restore power and switch on again.
technician: If nothing is blocking the fan and the code returns, request service.

Switch off the air conditioner's circuit breaker or unplug it.
Wait about 5 minutes, then restore power and switch on again.

causes: The internal water reservoir is full.
steps: Switch off and unplug the unit.
Drain the water from the drain port into a pan.
Refit the drain plug and restart the unit.
technician: If FL appears again right after draining, contact Haier service.

title: Tank full or float stuck (portable AC, 2016 and older)
causes: The water tank is full.

steps: Switch off and unplug the unit.

technician: If STOP stays with an empty tank and free float, contact Haier service.
